I have been farming these 12 mu for 25 years now. I finished middle school, so I can read the labels on fertilizer bags and talk to the seed dealer, but mostly I go by what I have seen work with my own eyes. Last year I had 5 mu of cotton, 3.5 mu of winter wheat, and 3.5 mu of summer maize, and that worked out fine, so I am not changing much this year.

For cotton, I plant the improved variety 99-1 that my cousin used two years ago and got good bolls from. I put 3 kg of seed per mu. For fertilizer, I lay down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — the 15-15-15 kind, about 180 yuan a bag — and then I topdress twice with urea, about 15 kg each time. That comes to around 22 kg of nitrogen per mu total, plus 8 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium from the compound. I know cotton is hungry, and two years ago I cut back and regretted it when the bolls were small, so I would rather spend a bit more than lose yield. I irrigate twice from my well, once at flowering and once at boll stage. Cotton pests are the worst — bollworm, aphids, spider mites — so I spray 15 times total, counting the herbicide at the start and the growth regulator at the end. I rotary till before planting. If the weather holds like last year, I expect 550 kg of seed cotton per mu.

For wheat, I plant the improved variety Jimai 22, 30 kg per mu. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing — the 18-22-5 kind the dealer says is good for wheat — and then in spring at green-up I spread 20 kg of urea per mu. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 2 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: once before winter, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I spray herbicide once, insecticide twice, and fungicide once — four times total. Rotary till before sowing. I expect about 1000 kg per mu.

For maize, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid, 1.2 kg per mu. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, 15-15-15, and topdress with 15 kg urea at the big trumpet stage. That is about 14 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu. I do not till for maize — I plant right after the wheat comes out in early June with the no-till planter the service team brings. Two irrigations, usually. Herbicide once and insecticide twice, three sprays total. Should get 1100 kg per mu if the rain cooperates.

My son works in the city and sends some money home, but my wife and I do most of the field work. For cotton picking and wheat harvest I might hire a few people or use the machine service. I have to watch my total spending — fertilizer prices went up again, and every bag is real money. But a bad harvest is worse than wasting a little fertilizer, so I stick with what worked last year and what my neighbors are doing. Most people around here use about the same amounts.
